clue.text: Novelist with baggage going to end of line

parts.note: baggage is an old disparaging word for a disreputable woman, a trollop

indicators.note: end of picks out only the final letter of the word line

explanation.surface: A writer heads for the railway terminus lugging a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baggage' looks like luggage but is the old insult for a loose woman. Anthony Trollope was the Victorian author of the Barchester novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthony Trollope was a prolific Victorian writer of fiction, an example of the category.

clue.text: Gossip with relation about empty teapot

indicators.note: about means the story is placed around the other letters

parts.note: a relation is an account or story, a tale

indicators.note: empty means the inside of teapot is removed, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone chatters about family over a teapot that has run dry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relation' suggests a relative, but here it means a story told, as in relating events.
explanation.definitionFit: To gossip and to tattle are synonyms: both mean to chatter idly about others' affairs.

clue.text: Monstrous female needs PR for advancement

indicators.note: the defined word needs the letters of PR to become the synonym, so those letters are taken away from it

parts.note: advancement means forward movement, progress
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fearsome woman hires a public relations team to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: PR looks like public relations, but the two letters simply need adding to the front of the answer to make the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A female ogre is the standard feminine form of the fairy-tale monster.

clue.text: Where Beatles started organ fund

parts.note: the liver is a bodily organ
a pool is a shared fund of money, as in a betting pool

explanation.surface: The band began by setting up a fund for body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beatles formed in the English port city of Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Liverpool is the birthplace of the Beatles, the location where the band formed.

clue.text: Celebrate lavishly and get ready for a row?

definitions.meaning: an idiom for spending freely on a celebration
taken literally, launching a boat before rowing it; the question mark flags the literal reading

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means spend generously on festivities, and literally describes launching a rowing boat.

clue.text: Musical interval not entirely for sea god

indicators.note: not entirely means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: a tritone is a musical interval of three whole tones

explanation.surface: A dissonant chord is only partly fit for a deity of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Triton is the Greek god of the sea, son of Poseidon, a proper-name example.

clue.text: Hindu sage getting letters from parishioners

indicators.note: letters from says a run of consecutive letters is taken out of the following word

explanation.surface: A holy man receives correspondence from members of a church congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rishi is an inspired poet or seer in Hindu tradition, a synonym for a holy wise man.

clue.text: Stimulated but knocked out in round ten

indicators.note: knocked out signals that the letters are bashed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: A boxer felt excited despite being flattened in the tenth round.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a boxing match, so 'knocked out' reads as a knockout; it is the signal to rearrange the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aroused or excited by something is the idiomatic sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Underwriters take time out with one similarly entitled

parts.note: Names are the private individuals who underwrite insurance at Lloyd's of London

indicators.note: out means the letter for time is dropped from the word take

explanation.surface: Insurers take a break, accompanied by someone with the same job title.
explanation.walkthrough: Lloyd's of London is the British insurance market whose backers are called Names.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sharing the same name as another is so called; entitled here means bearing the same title.

clue.text: Roman residents rioting in Paris area

indicators.note: rioting suggests the letters running wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: Inhabitants of Rome are causing disorder in a district of the French capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is divided into twenty administrative districts, each called by this French term.

clue.text: Having even discarded T-shirt, American composer does well

indicators.note: having the even-numbered letters thrown away leaves the first, third and fifth letters of the word

parts.note: Charles Ives was a modernist American composer

explanation.surface: A US musician succeeds even after throwing away his casual top.
explanation.walkthrough: From T-SHIRT the odd letters T, H, R remain once the even ones are discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish or prosper is a synonym for doing well.

clue.text: Men coming back to play guitars on platform

indicators.note: coming back means the two letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
to strum is to play a guitar by sweeping the strings

explanation.surface: Musicians return to the stage to play their guitars.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand for a speaker or conductor, a synonym for a dais.

clue.text: One doesn't succeed in close race

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Somebody fails to win a tightly contested race.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fails to win is by definition the opposite of a winner.

clue.text: Unfaithful partners watch clock?

definitions.meaning: people who cheat on their lovers
a watch and a clock are a pair of timekeeping devices, read literally

explanation.definitionFit: Cheating partners are so called, and a watch and a clock are literally a pair of timekeepers.

clue.text: Dodos may be OK playing old record

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters romping about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder
taken as written as fodder

explanation.surface: Extinct birds may be fine frolicking around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Playing' rearranges DODOSMAYBE into DOMESDAYBO, with OK left standing at the end. The Domesday Book is William the Conqueror's 1086 survey of England.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the 1086 survey of English landholding, an ancient written register.

clue.text: Tuna or bass finely cooked outside

indicators.note: outside means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
cooked suggests the letters are prepared and transformed into a new order

parts.note: a bass voice or note is low

explanation.surface: A fish dish where sea bass is finely prepared on the exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooked' turns the letters of finely into YELFIN, split around the middle piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellowfin is a large species of tuna caught in warm seas.

clue.text: Upturned food containers needed by Elvis for eating between meals?

indicators.note: upturned in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: cans are tins that hold food
Elvis Presley was known as the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: Elvis needs overturned tins of food for his between-meal treats.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a light bite outside regular mealtimes is what the verb describes.

clue.text: Exalted university given tribute

parts.note: given tribute means praised

explanation.surface: A college was honoured with tributes and raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: Raised high or elevated is a synonym for exalted.

clue.text: Two card games played by Robert Vaughn

parts.note: Napoleon, or nap, is a trick-taking card game
solo, or solo whist, is another card game

explanation.surface: An actor sits down to a couple of hands of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Vaughn played the spy Napoleon Solo in the 1960s TV series The Man from U.N.C.L.E.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon Solo was the agent character the actor portrayed in a 1960s spy series.

clue.text: After a little while Lincoln's given up simple life

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a little while

indicators.note: given up in a down clue means the name is read upwards

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: After a short time, Lincoln has surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoeba is a single-celled organism, an example of a very basic form of life.

clue.text: Swimming in Calder: situation far from grave

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters floating about into a new order

explanation.surface: Bathing in a river, someone finds their position anything but serious.
explanation.walkthrough: The Calder is a river in northern England. The definition plays on the phrase 'from the cradle to the grave'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from the cradle to the grave makes the infant's bed the starting point, as far from the tomb as life gets.

clue.text: Bronte associated with the Web?

definitions.meaning: one of the three novelist sisters, author of Jane Eyre
the spider in the children's book ... Web, by E. B. White

explanation.definitionFit: It is the first name of the Jane Eyre author and of the spider in E. B. White's novel.

clue.text: True ally when tortured admitting nothing

indicators.note: admitting means the rearranged letters take in another piece
when tortured suggests the letters are twisted into a new shape

parts.note: O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A faithful friend under torture confesses nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being faithful and steadfast is a synonym for being true to someone.

clue.text: First mentioned (but not first) seashell

indicators.note: but not first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the former is the first of two things mentioned

explanation.surface: A shell is named first, but then demoted from first place.
explanation.walkthrough: The ormer is an abalone found in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an edible mollusc, the abalone, so its shell is a type of seashell.

clue.text: Quizmaster's explanation of his role? Really!

definitions.meaning: a quizmaster's job is literally to put questions to people

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation expresses exasperation, and literally states what a quiz host does.

clue.text: Men not married, runners in London borough

indicators.note: not means the married letter is taken away from the word men

parts.note: the field is all the runners in a race

explanation.surface: Single men compete as racers in a part of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Enfield is a borough in north London.
explanation.definitionFit: Enfield is one of the outer boroughs of Greater London, an example of the category.

clue.text: Good US lawyer about to get away from troublemaker

indicators.note: about means the two letters are turned round

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor
to fly is to flee or get away

explanation.surface: A decent American attorney is about to escape from a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a persistent irritant or provocateur, a synonym for a troublemaker.

clue.text: Very old individual in step

indicators.note: in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a stage is a step in a process
an individual is one person

explanation.surface: A single person keeps in step.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone Age is the prehistoric period, so used adjectivally it means ancient or very old.
